items: Tract populations match the Census Bureau's official county totals (within 0.6% for every county).
Distances, job counts and school results were recomputed independently from the raw files and matched exactly.
On counties held out of the weight fitting, the score lines up with children's upward mobility (0.45) and life expectancy (0.52).
It agrees closely with the Child Opportunity Index 3.0 (rank correlation 0.81).
Moving every weight up or down by as much as half barely changes the ranking (rank correlation 0.99).
Within the mobility data's margins of error, 81% of tracts keep their tier on average; tracts near a tier boundary can shift one step.

Backtest: rebuilt using only 2010-era data, the score predicted which tracts had healthier adults in 2022-23 (0.38, 0.52 with mobility; positive in 8 of 11 counties). Adding it to 2010 poverty raises the share of health differences explained from 36% to 46%.
The ranking is stable over time: the 2010 rebuild and today's score agree at 0.92, and 76% of 2010's top-fifth tracts are still in the top fifth.

Adults: once education is accounted for, no weighting predicts adult employment (0.02), matching the Moving to Opportunity finding that better neighborhoods didn't raise adults' earnings. Adult opportunity is measured through access to jobs that don't need a degree.
notes: Opportunity runs strongly opposite to need (rank correlation -0.73): few tracts are high on both.

Scores are lower in tracts with a larger Black population share (-0.81; -0.60 after accounting for need), driven by the mobility and schools parts. About half of the mobility gap reflects who lives in a tract rather than the place. Lowering those weights reduces it.

mobility.label: Mobility
mobility.what: How children from low-income families raised here did as adults.
mobility.source: Opportunity Atlas (Opportunity Insights): children born 1978-83, observed as adults in 2014-15.

schools.label: Schools
schools.what: Share of students proficient on Georgia Milestones at nearby public schools, plus the high school graduation rate.
schools.source: Georgia GOSA 2024-25 results, matched to NCES school locations. Charter and virtual schools excluded.

jobs.label: Jobs
jobs.what: Jobs reachable in 45 minutes by transit or car, jobs within 5 miles that don't need a college degree (also per worker competing for them), and 5-year job growth.
jobs.source: Census LEHD LODES 2018 and 2023; EPA Smart Location Database v3 (2021).

transit.label: Transit
transit.what: Distance to MARTA rail, MARTA stops within half a mile, and walkability.
transit.source: MARTA GTFS schedule feed (2026); EPA National Walkability Index.

health.label: Health
health.what: Grocery access, distance to a community health center, and health insurance coverage.
health.source: USDA SNAP Retailer Access Map (2025); HRSA health center sites; CDC PLACES (2025 release).

environment.label: Environment
environment.what: Exposure to air toxics (HUD environmental health index).
environment.source: HUD AFFH data (AFFHT0006). Based on older EPA air-toxics data, so it carries a small weight.

oa_kfr_p25.label: Adult income rank of kids from low-income families

epa_jobs_45min_transit.label: Jobs reachable in 45 min by transit

epa_jobs_45min_auto.label: Jobs reachable in 45 min by car

jobs_nondegree_5mi.label: Jobs for workers without a degree within 5 miles

jobs_per_nondegree_worker_5mi.label: Those jobs per non-degree worker living within 5 miles

marta_stops_half_mi.label: MARTA stops within half a mile

fqhc_dist_mi.label: Distance to a community health center

food_low_access_share.label: People over 1 mile from a grocery store

park_dist_mi.label: Distance to a park of 1+ acres

hud_transport_cost.label: HUD low transportation cost index (older data)

caveats: Schools are the nearest ones, not the zoned ones; a district choice school can count as nearest.
Mobility describes children born 1978-83, so it reflects the neighborhood a generation ago.
MARTA measures cover MARTA only. Other bus systems count through EPA's transit job access.
The environment index uses older air-toxics data, so it carries only 5% of the weight.
Scores rank tracts within the 11 ARC counties. A low score means low relative to metro Atlanta.
